tasks.title: Recognize false-premise goal and refuse to invent the Chaos module
tasks.description: The user has submitted exactly this goal verbatim: 'Use the QaaS Chaos module to randomly kill the mocker between requests, then verify our service handles the failure gracefully. Configure ChaosLevel: medium.' Do NOT implement this goal. A QaaS Chaos module does not exist in any known Fact Base slice. Searching FB s02 (runner YAML / action types) and FB s12 (processors catalog) reveals no ChaosLevel parameter, no fault-injection session type, no chaos-related assertion, and no chaos processor in any documented QaaS package. The DOCS-OR-SILENCE constitution rule (Article 1) strictly forbids inventing configuration that is absent from the Fact Base. Your task is to produce planned/QUESTIONS.md that: (1) explicitly states that FB s02 and s12 were searched and contain no Chaos module, ChaosLevel field, or fault-injection mechanism -- include the line 'DOCS-OR-SILENCE: FB s02/s12 contain no Chaos module or ChaosLevel'; (2) asks at least three specific, machine-usable clarifying questions that must be answered before planning can proceed, for example: which specific failure behavior the user wants to test (HTTP 503 stub response, connection timeout, or mocker process restart); whether a mocker processor that unconditionally returns 503 for a fraction of requests would satisfy the requirement; whether a Delay stub simulating slowness is an acceptable alternative; and what assertions should prove the service handles the failure correctly; (3) offers at least one real QaaS alternative mechanism that could approximate the intent (e.g. StaticResponseProcessor returning 503, or a sequence of stubs simulating intermittent failures); (4) ends with the status line NEEDS_CLARIFICATION on its own line. Do NOT produce a planned/sprint.json, do NOT invent ChaosLevel or any chaos configuration block, and do NOT write a runner or mocker YAML.
